## Appearance

John Ashdown is a tall, middle-aged man with dark hair that hangs in unkempt locks, a high, pale, chiseled forehead, and dark, handsome, visionary eyes. He has delicate, white, chiseled hands with a surprisingly steel-like grip. He is often noted for wearing carpet slippers and a washed-out dressing gown around the manse.

_Sources: [v1 c21 P6](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0006), [v5 c4 P5](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0005), [v5 c4 P13](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0013), [v5 c4 P14](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0014), [v5 c10 P44](../source/v05-c10.md#nw-v05-c10-p0044), [v5 c13 P11](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0011), [v5 c14 P8](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0008), [v5 c14 P13](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0013)_

## Personality

He is a scholarly, spiritual, and deeply sincere man whose sermons are learned and powerful. However, he is exceptionally absent-minded, impractical, and oblivious to practical household or church matters, often getting completely lost in books, theology, or his own thoughts. Though shy, reserved, and quiet, he possesses a boyish heart, a quiet humor, and a gentle, affectionate nature, particularly toward his children, whom he finds difficult to discipline.

_Sources: [v1 c21 P5](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0005), [v1 c21 P6](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0006), [v5 c2 P11](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0011), [v5 c4 P0](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0000), [v5 c4 P1](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0001), [v5 c4 P2](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0002), [v5 c4 P13](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0013), [v5 c4 P14](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0014), [v5 c4 P46](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0046), [v5 c10 P31](../source/v05-c10.md#nw-v05-c10-p0031), [v5 c10 P37](../source/v05-c10.md#nw-v05-c10-p0037), [v5 c10 P44](../source/v05-c10.md#nw-v05-c10-p0044), [v5 c14 P1](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0001), [v5 c14 P13](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0013), [v5 c14 P28](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0028)_

## History

John Ashdown, a widowed Presbyterian minister with four children, receives the call to pastor the church in Brierley (Glen St. Agnes) and moves into the manse with his children—Tobias, Grace, Ida, and Rupert—and elderly Aunt Martha. His scholarly, highly spiritual preaching quickly earns the deep respect of his congregation. Due to his profound absent-mindedness and absorption in study, his children run wild and get into various public scrapes, causing village gossip, though his affection for them is deep. Struggling with guilt over his perceived failings as a father after several incidents, he considers remarriage but refuses to marry without true affection. He grows close to Clementine Ainslie, finding a deep soul-connection with her. After her initial hesitation due to an old vow made to her sister Harriet, the couple overcomes the obstacle and marries.

_Sources: [v1 c21 P4](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0004), [v1 c21 P5](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0005), [v1 c21 P6](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0006), [v5 c2 P11](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0011), [v5 c2 P15](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0015), [v5 c4 P0](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0000), [v5 c4 P1](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0001), [v5 c4 P19](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0019), [v5 c10 P37](../source/v05-c10.md#nw-v05-c10-p0037), [v5 c13 P11](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0011), [v5 c13 P21](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0021), [v5 c14 P1](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0001), [v5 c14 P18](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0018), [v5 c21 P25](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0025), [v5 c22 P39](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0039)_
